chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Sulayman ibn Harun, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about making up the prayer after the 'Asr prayer. He said, 'Yes, they are merely the voluntary prayers, so make them up whenever you wish.'

key_terms.قَضَاءِ: making up a missed obligatory act

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up the 'Asr prayer and when can it be performed?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the makeup of the 'Asr prayer is treated as *nawafil* (voluntary), thereby exempting it from the strict prohibitions of *karahat* times that typically apply to obligatory prayers. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the ritual status of *qada* (makeup) and the original *ada* (on-time) prayer, allowing flexibility in performance. It underscores the practical ease granted to believers for fulfilling missed obligations without the burden of timing restrictions.
